reason: The cited evidence broadly supports the general promise of HEAs and the role of precipitates for high-temperature strength (E1, E11), but no passage provides specific evidence for the central mechanistic claim that a tunable entropy-enthalpy competition governs the simultaneous optimization of all four target properties (high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, cryogenic toughness) in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni. The hypothesis overstates the support, as the cited evidence is largely generic or addresses only subsets of the claimed properties and mechanisms.
premises: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs is governed by a competition between mixing entropy and enthalpy of formation of secondary phases.
Adjusting composition and processing conditions can control this entropy-enthalpy competition.
Controlling this competition can achieve a balance of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
The formation of secondary phases (e.g., precipitates) is the structural mediator linking composition/processing to properties.
The cited evidence demonstrates that Al+Ti additions form γ′ precipitates which improve high-temperature strength and stability.
